```{r}
library(readxl)
library(fmsb)
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
# Load the Excel file
file_path <- "./confusion_matrices_scores.xlsx" # Update this to the path of your Excel file
sheet_names <- excel_sheets(file_path)

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the performance metrics
performance_df <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 5, nrow = 0))
colnames(performance_df) <- c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "GEM")

# Loop through each sheet (GEM) and load the performance metrics
for (sheet_name in sheet_names) {
  data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name)
  # Replace NA values with zero
  data[is.na(data)] <- 0
  performance_metrics <- data[1, c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1")]  # Excluding MCC
  # Remove "ttmodel_" from GEM names
  cleaned_name <- gsub("ttmodel_", "", sheet_name)
  performance_metrics$GEM <- cleaned_name
  performance_df <- rbind(performance_df, performance_metrics)
}

# Add max and min values for each metric for plotting
max_values <- c(1, 1, 1, 1, "max")
min_values <- c(0, 0, 0, 0, "min")
performance_df <- rbind(performance_df, max_values, min_values)

# Convert the GEM column to row names
rownames(performance_df) <- performance_df$GEM
performance_df$GEM <- NULL

# Ensure all data is numeric
performance_df <- apply(performance_df, 2, as.numeric)

# Creating the radar chart
radarchart <- radarchart(as.data.frame(t(performance_df)), axistype = 1, 
                         paxislabels = c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1"), 
                         title = "Performance Metrics of GEMs",
                         vlcex = 0.8)

print(radarchart)

```


```{r}
library(readxl)
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# Load the Excel file
file_path <- "./confusion_matrices_scores.xlsx" # Update this to the path of your Excel file
sheet_names <- excel_sheets(file_path)

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the performance metrics
performance_df <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 5, nrow = 0))
colnames(performance_df) <- c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1", "GEM")

# Loop through each sheet (GEM) and load the performance metrics
for (sheet_name in sheet_names) {
  data <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = sheet_name)
  # Replace NA values with zero
  data[is.na(data)] <- 0
  performance_metrics <- data[1, c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Recall", "F1")]  # Excluding MCC
  # Remove "ttmodel_" from GEM names
  cleaned_name <- gsub("ttmodel_", "", sheet_name)
  performance_metrics$GEM <- cleaned_name
  performance_df <- rbind(performance_df, performance_metrics)
}

# Convert the data frame to long format
performance_long <- performance_df %>%
  gather(key = "Metric", value = "Value", -GEM)

# Create a list of radar charts, one for each GEM
radar_charts <- performance_long %>%
  split(.$GEM) %>%
  map(~plot_ly(data = ., type = 'scatterpolar', fill = 'toself') %>%
        add_trace(r = ~Value, theta = ~Metric) %>%
        layout(polar = list(radialaxis = list(visible = T, range = c(0, 1))), 
               showlegend = F, title = ~unique(.x$GEM)))

# Show the radar chart for the first GEM (change the index to view others)
radar_charts[[1]]
```


```{r}
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Radar Charts of GEMs"),
  selectInput("gem", "Choose a GEM:", choices = names(radar_charts)),
  plotlyOutput("radarChart")
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$radarChart <- renderPlotly({
    radar_charts[[input$gem]]
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

```

```{r}
# Defining a set of distinct colors manually

distinct_colors <- c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A", "#984EA3", "#FF7F00", "#FFFF33", "#A65628", "#F781BF", "#999999", "#66C2A5", "#FC8D62", "#8DA0CB", "#E78AC3", "#A6D854", "#FFD92F", "#E5C494", "#B3B3B3","#E7298A")

# Ensure there are enough colors for all GEMs
if(length(distinct_colors) < length(names(radar_charts))) {
  stop("Not enough colors provided for all GEMs. Please add more colors to the 'distinct_colors' vector.")
}

# Creating a single radar chart with all GEMs
radar_chart_all <- plot_ly(type = 'scatterpolar', fill = 'toself') %>%
  layout(
    polar = list(radialaxis = list(visible = T, range = c(0, 1))),
    title = list(text = "Confusion Matrix Metrics", x = 0, xanchor = "left"),
    showlegend = TRUE
  )

# Add each GEM as a trace to the radar chart
for (i in seq_along(names(radar_charts))) {
  gem <- names(radar_charts)[i]
  radar_chart_all <- radar_chart_all %>%
    add_trace(
      data = performance_long %>% filter(GEM == gem),
      r = ~Value, theta = ~Metric,
      name = gem,
      line = list(color = distinct_colors[i])
    )
}

# Show the radar chart
radar_chart_all
```

```{r}
# Number of GEMs
num_gems <- length(names(radar_charts))

# Creating a set of distinct colors using the rainbow function
distinct_colors <- rainbow(num_gems)

# Creating a single radar chart with all GEMs
radar_chart_all <- plot_ly(type = 'scatterpolar', fill = 'toself') %>%
layout(
  polar = list(
    domain = list(x = c(0.1, 0.9), y = c(0.1, 0.9)),
    radialaxis = list(
      visible = T, 
      range = c(0, 1), 
      tickfont = list(size = 50, weight = "bold")
    ),
    angularaxis = list(tickfont = list(size = 70, color = "black"))
  ),
  showlegend = TRUE,
  legend = list(font = list(size = 43, color = "black"))
)

# Add each GEM as a trace to the radar chart
for (i in seq_along(names(radar_charts))) {
  gem <- names(radar_charts)[i]
  radar_chart_all <- radar_chart_all %>%
    add_trace(
      data = performance_long %>% filter(GEM == gem),
      r = ~Value, theta = ~Metric,
      name = gem,
      line = list(color = distinct_colors[i]),
      textfont = list(size = 24)
    )
}

# Show the radar chart
radar_chart_all

```
